# Exact base-tilt quotas for an actual propagated critical cap

This is a finite-epsilon consequence of actual cap minimality at EACH
deepest source. It is stronger than the averaged section-centroid
identity of one selected separator. It neither chooses new supporting
allocations nor replaces the original cap menu.

## 1. One cap and its actual statuses

Let C have finitely many positive convex d-fibers K_z, d>=1.
Fix a closed cap H={a·z+u·x>=b}, u nonzero, which is an actual
mass-Q minimizing buffered cap at every source Y_p=(p,y_p)
under consideration. In particular

    b=a·p+u·y_p-epsilon f(Y_p)Gamma(u).

For this fixed cap, let

    S_z=H_(d-1)(K_z intersect boundary H)/|u|

at every proper fiber trace. At an outside-supporting trace, where
K_z lies in the closed complement of H, let A_z be its supporting
facet area divided by |u|. At an inside-supporting trace, where
K_z lies in H, let B_z be the same coarea. Lower-dimensional exposed
faces have zero coarea when d>1. In d=1 these are the usual endpoint
counting coareas. Strictly full and strictly empty fibers contribute
zero.

For a source p and any base direction v, perturb the base normal to
a+t v while retaining u, the source, the body and epsilon. The
buffered threshold becomes b+t v·p, since Gamma(u) and f(Y_p)
are unchanged. In fiber z the margin therefore increases by
t v·(z-p).

The exact right derivative of cap mass is

    D_p(v)=sum_proper S_z v·(z-p)
       +sum_outside A_z [v·(z-p)]_+
       +sum_inside B_z [v·(z-p)]_-,                    (1)

where r_+=max(r,0), r_-=min(r,0).
Every term comes from the actual cap response. At an outside facet,
positive displacement admits a thin layer and negative displacement
does nothing. At an inside facet, negative displacement removes a
thin layer and positive displacement does nothing. Proper traces
have the ordinary section derivative.

For completeness these statements follow directly from Fubini in the
u direction. The (d-1)-dimensional section areas converge to their
proper value at an interior level and to the exposed facet area at a
supporting endpoint. The one-sided shell thickness is
t|v·(z-p)|/|u|. There are finitely many fibers, so the derivatives add.
No general-position assumption is used.

Because the old cap is minimizing at the source,

    D_p(v)>=0 for EVERY base v.                        (2)

These are exact finite-epsilon inequalities. They have no O(epsilon)
error: this variation does not move the continuous normal or buffer.

## 2. A source-width quota in every base direction

Choose two actual sources p,q and a base direction v with
a_0=v·p<b_0=v·q. Write s_z=v·z and S=sum_proper S_z.
Apply (2) at p with direction -v, and at q with direction v.
After cancellation of the proper first moment, their sum gives

    (b_0-a_0) S
      +sum_inside B_z[(s_z-a_0)_+ +(b_0-s_z)_+]
    <=sum_outside A_z[(a_0-s_z)_+ +(s_z-b_0)_+].       (3)

The inside contribution is nonnegative. The right side uses ONLY
outside-supporting fibers whose projected bases lie strictly beyond
the source slab [a_0,b_0]. Supporting fibers between the sources
cannot pay this quota.

In particular, if all source bases lie in a hull B, choose p,q
attaining its width in direction v. A propagated cap with positive
proper source coarea must have an actual outside-supporting fiber
on at least one side beyond this slab. It cannot be proper or merely
inside-supporting on all positive fibers.

For n=1, source endpoints a<b give the especially concrete form

    (b-a)sum_proper S_z
      +sum_inside,z>a B_z(z-a)
      +sum_inside,z<b B_z(b-z)
    <=sum_outside,z<a A_z(a-z)
      +sum_outside,z>b A_z(z-b).                      (4)

Thus inside-supporting incidences make the requirement strictly
harder whenever their coarea is positive.

## 3. Exact pointed scaling on a homothetic source interval

Assume the actual propagated one-group envelope

    K_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D

with affine y and positive affine ell, and equality on the whole
source interval B=[a,b]. The common cap equation is

    u·xi+c=0,       xi=(x-y(z))/ell(z).

Let

    s_D=H_(d-1)(D intersect {u·xi+c=0})/|u|>0.

Every sampled source base in B is proper, and

    S_z=ell(z)^(d-1) s_D,      z in B intersect Z.     (5)

At an outside-supporting fiber its pointed facet is contained in
the same section of D, so

    0<=A_z<=ell(z)^(d-1)s_D.                          (6)

Consequently (4) implies the useful arithmetic necessary condition

    (b-a)sum_(z in B intersect Z)ell(z)^(d-1)
       <=sum_(outside,z<a)ell(z)^(d-1)(a-z)
          +sum_(outside,z>b)ell(z)^(d-1)(z-b).          (7)

Discarding proper sections outside B and the inside penalty only
weakens the exact quota. Equation (7) holds separately for every
selected actual cap; its outside-support sets are geometric data
of that cap, not freely chosen labels.

## 4. The cap menu must use both outside directions when n=1

For fixed pointed xi, the set of real bases satisfying
(z,y(z)+ell(z)xi) in C is an interval, because that physical map is
affine in z. It contains B. Therefore the pointed fibers D_z are
nested decreasing along each side away from B.

If a cap has an outside-supporting fiber on the right of B, every
farther-right pointed fiber lies in its closed complement. The
analogous statement holds on the left.

Now take the actual finite H menu. Its pointed margins satisfy

    sum_j rho_j[u_j·xi+epsilon f_D Gamma(u_j)]
       =epsilon f_D[1+a_D·xi]>0 on D.                  (8)

Thus the cap complements have empty common intersection in D.
If EVERY cap had an outside support somewhere on the right, the
last sampled positive fiber would lie in every such complement,
contradicting (8). Hence some cap has no right outside support.
By its positive quota (4), that cap has a left outside support.
Similarly some cap has a right outside support and no left one.

This proves a genuine two-sided incidence requirement for the
actual menu. It does not say that every cap has both types of
support, that proper-section means lie inside B, or that the
resulting incidence measures already pay Gamma_d/2.

## 5. Outside support on either side is a single endpoint facet

For n=1, an actual cap can have at most one outside-supporting
sampled fiber on each side of B. Indeed C intersect H is a
full-dimensional convex body: proper source cap fibers at two
different source bases give full ambient dimension. Every interior
base of its projection has a positive d-volume section. An
outside-supporting fiber has nonempty cap intersection but zero
d-volume, so its base is an endpoint of that projection.

An elementary alternative avoids even the full-dimensional-section
statement. If two outside supports had bases z_1<z_2<a, interpolate
a point on the cap boundary at z_1 with a small above-plane ball
in a proper source fiber at a. At base z_2 the interpolation gives
an above-plane ball, contradicting outside support there.
The right-side argument is identical. Apply the same reasoning to
the complementary closed halfspace to get the corresponding
uniqueness for inside-supporting bases.

Thus the right side of (4) consists of at most two actual facet
coareas at genuine endpoint bases.

## 6. A new source-width restriction from ordinary section concavity

Under the hypotheses of Section 4, the integer source interval
cannot have width m=b-a>=d. Consequently, when it contains an
interior integer witness,

    2<=b-a<=d-1.                                      (9)

In particular this full-rank occupied-interval one-group configuration
is impossible for d=1 or d=2, without any constant-scale or smoothness
assumption.

Proof. Choose the actual menu cap with left outside support and no
right outside support, whose existence was proved in Section 4.
By Section 5 its positive outside coarea is concentrated at one
integer base L<a. Put h=b-L, so h>=m+1, and write A=A_L>0.
Dropping the nonnegative inside terms from (4) gives

    m sum_proper S_z <= A(a-L)=A(h-m).                 (10)

Every fiber at a real base strictly between L and b is proper for
this cap. For the above-plane part interpolate a boundary point in
K_L with an interior above-plane ball in K_b. For the below-plane
part interpolate below-plane interior balls in K_L and K_b.
Both produce a positive-radius ball at every intermediate base.
In particular all sampled L+1,...,b are proper.

For d>=2, take affine continuous coordinates on the moving cap
plane. Its sections are compatible (d-1)-dimensional convex bodies.
Brunn--Minkowski, keeping only the contribution of the endpoint
facet at L, gives

    S_z >= A[(b-z)/h]^(d-1),       L<z<b.

The coarea divisor |u| is fixed and causes no change to this
homogeneous inequality. Hence (10) implies

    m sum_(j=1)^(h-1) (j/h)^(d-1) <= h-m.             (11)

If m>=d>=2, monotonicity of t^(d-1) and strict Bernoulli give

    sum_(j=1)^(h-1)(j/h)^(d-1)
      > integral_0^(h-1)(t/h)^(d-1)dt
      = (h/d)(1-1/h)^d
      > h/d-1.

Multiplying by m gives a quantity strictly greater than
(m/d)h-m>=h-m, contradicting (11).

For d=1 every proper section and every endpoint facet has the same
coarea 1/|u|. There are at least h proper sampled sections
L+1,...,b. Equation (10) would give m h<=h-m, impossible for m>=1.
This completes all cases.

The proof uses actual common-Q cap minimality at the endpoints,
the full finite-epsilon cap cover, and compatible sections. It does
not follow from generic sampled-envelope geometry or from an
arbitrary imposed section-centroid condition.
